title: Whole-number long division and remainders
intro: Long division builds a quotient one place at a time. Each chosen digit must fit the current amount without using more than is available.
html:
Whole-number long division and remainders

Long division builds a quotient one place at a time. Each chosen digit must fit the current amount without using more than is available.

After dividing and subtracting, bring down the next digit. A zero may be needed in the quotient. A remainder records what is left and must be smaller than the divisor.

A method to try

  1. Estimate the first quotient digit from the leftmost usable digits.
  2. Multiply, subtract and bring down the next digit; repeat for every place.
  3. Check dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder, with remainder smaller than divisor.

Worked examples

49161 ÷ 35

35 × 1400 = 49000, leaving 161. Four more groups use 140, leaving 21.

49161 ÷ 35 = 1404 R 21

Check: 35 × 1404 + 21 = 49161, and 21 < 35.

A mistake to watch for

Do not drop an interior zero from 1404. Do not include another full group when fewer than 35 objects remain.

Check and explain

In a packing story, label full groups and leftover objects separately.
examples: 35 × 1400 = 49000, leaving 161. Four more groups use 140, leaving 21.
